question: Who among the following was the first independent Gupta king to hold the title of Maharajadhiraj?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandragupta I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Chandragupta I was the first independent Gupta king to hold the title of Maharajadhiraj, which means "King of Kings".
 
• His reign marked the beginning of the Gupta Empire's expansion, which is often referred to as the Golden Age of India due to significant achievements in arts, science, and political administration.
 
• Chandragupta I ruled from circa 320 to 335 CE, succeeding his father, Ghatotkach Gupta.
 
• He strengthened his position and extended his empire through matrimonial alliances, notably by marrying Kumaradevi, a Lichchhavi princess.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gupta Empire**

 
 
• The Gupta Empire was an ancient Indian empire that existed from approximately 320 to 550 CE.
 
• It is known for a period of prosperity and cultural flourishing, particularly in fields such as literature, architecture, and sciences.
 
• The period of Gupta rule is often referred to as the Golden Age of India.
 
 
 
• **Chandragupta I's Contributions**
 
 
• Chandragupta I's reign laid the foundation for the future expansion and consolidation of the Gupta Empire.
 
• His strategic matrimonial alliances bolstered the empire's political strength and stability.
 
 
 
• **Successors**
 
 
• Chandragupta I was succeeded by his son, Samudragupta, who expanded the empire through military conquests.
 
• Samudragupta is often considered one of the greatest rulers of the Gupta dynasty.
 
 
 
• **Historical Sources**
 
 
• Information about Chandragupta I and the Gupta Empire comes from various sources, including inscriptions, coins, and contemporary literary works.
 
• Archaeological findings have also provided insights into the Gupta period's socio-economic and cultural life.
